llm.summary: The skill claims a full PhD research lifecycle (including web search/downloading and many helper scripts) but the package is incomplete and contains multiple broken/incoherent scripts — not clearly malicious, but inconsistent and risky to run without review and sandboxing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a full lifecycle (project init, multi-source paper search & download, paper analysis, experiment design generation, init_research_project.py, multi_source_search.py, paper_analyzer.py, create_experiment_design.py, etc.), yet the package only contains four scripts (check_compliance.py, generate_latex_template.py, revision_tracker.py, verify_math_notation.py). Several major capabilities advertised (searching/downloading from arXiv/IEEE/Semantic Scholar, init scripts, experiment automation) are referenced but their implementations are absent. This is a clear mismatch between advertised purpose and actual code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions in SKILL.md instruct running many scripts (including missing ones). The included scripts that do exist perform file system reads/writes inside a user-specified project directory, export/modify compliance JSON files, and attempt to create or update '00-dashboard' or compliance files via relative paths (e.g., '../../00-dashboard/compliance-status.json'), which could point outside the skill folder depending on the supplied project-dir. The instructions do not request or document network credentials despite promising multi-source downloads, so it's unclear how external services would be accessed. Several instructions reference files that are not present, which may lead an agent to try to run non-existent commands or to improvise — increasing risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only with code files). That minimizes installation-time risk — nothing is declared to be downloaded or executed automatically by an installer. The main risk comes from executing the included Python scripts directly.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package declares no required environment variables or credentials. However SKILL.md claims access to external scholarly sources (arXiv, IEEE Xplore, Semantic Scholar) but the repository does not include network client code or require API keys, creating an inconsistency: either the networked parts are missing, or the tool expects the agent/user to provide credentials or custom scripts not present. The existing scripts primarily read/write local project files and compliance JSON; they do not declare any external credentials, which is proportionate for those functions but inconsistent with the advertised web search/download features.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not declare system-wide privileges. The included scripts write and update files inside a project tree and attempt to read/write dashboard/compliance JSON files via relative paths; this is normal for project management tools but could modify files outside the skill folder depending on the project-dir argument. There is no indication the skill modifies other skills' configs or requests permanent system-level presence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Major mismatch: The README/SKILL.md advertises many scripts (init_research_project.py, multi_source_search.py, paper_analyzer.py, create_experiment_design.py) that are not present. Treat the package as incomplete — it likely won't deliver the advertised full functionality.

- Broken/buggy code: The included Python scripts contain numerous syntax and logical errors (invalid imports/variables, malformed f-strings, bad Path usage, undefined names, broken JSON/file handling). These bugs mean running the scripts will likely crash or behave unpredictably.

- File-write behavior: Several scripts attempt to read/write compliance/dashboard JSON and write reports using relative paths (e.g., '../../00-dashboard/compliance-status.json'). If you run these against a real project directory, the scripts may create/overwrite files outside the skill folder. To be safe, do not point the tools at important data — use an isolated test directory.

- Missing network/auth pieces: The SKILL.md promises multi-source paper downloads and analysis, but no downloader/network code or API-key requirements are present. If the missing functionality is added later, it could require API keys or external network access; verify where those keys would be stored and who can read them.

- How to proceed safely:
  - Do NOT run these scripts on your real research workspace or with your main project directory. Instead, inspect/fix the code locally and run it inside a disposable container, VM, or dedicated sandbox with no network and only test files.
  - Ask the publisher/owner for the missing files, a source repository (homepage/Git), and a changelog. A trustworthy skill should link to a source repo and release notes.
  - If you must run anything: run static linters (flake8/mypy), review the code for the specific paths that will be written, and run in a container with a temporary project-dir to observe behavior.
  - If you expect networked paper downloads, require the skill to explicitly declare which credentials or API endpoints it needs and show code that performs the downloads (so you can review any external endpoints).

Given the incomplete and buggy state, treat this skill as untrusted until the author provides a complete, corrected codebase and a source/homepage. If you want, I can produce a short checklist of minimal fixes/reviews an author should apply before it's safe to run.
